finding: Held: second attempt, closer but not ready to publish. There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so there is nothing to call too wide or too narrow; this is a first build. Built totals for one hose (part + stated hours x $120-$160 an hour, the national middle labor rate used for these checks), coolant not included: economy 2015 Toyota Corolla about $79-$152 ($19.49 Gates hose to $39.74 genuine, 0.5-0.7 hr); midsize 2016 Chevrolet Malibu 1.5L about $79-$274 ($19.49 Gates hose to $162.16 genuine, 0.5-0.7 hr); truck 2015 Ram 1500 5.7L about $144-$427 ($83.54 Gates hose to $107.00 genuine, 0.5-2 hr); luxury 2015 BMW 328i from about $109 ($48.99 Rein hose + 0.5 hr x $120), with no top because no top labor time was found (the genuine hose is $154.45 at list). The midsize example was changed from the Honda CR-V to the Malibu because the Malibu has a maker-stated time. How solid the labor times are, stated plainly. The one maker figure is GM bulletin 17-NA-120 for the 2016-2017 Malibu 1.5L: 'Add Radiator Outlet Hose 0.7 hr'. It names only the hose and prints a unit, but it is an add-on time paid on top of a radiator bracket repair, so it is not quite a stand-alone time, and as a warranty time it is the low end of what a shop bills. It is the top of the range for the Malibu and, as a comparable four-cylinder front-drive sedan from another maker, for the Corolla; it was not applied to the BMW. The low end everywhere is a general guide's statement that one hose usually takes less than 30 minutes, written for an owner and not for any vehicle. The truck's top is a parts seller's 2-hour installation time for an upper hose on the example truck, also written for an owner; the same seller says 1 hour for an older Ram. Cross-checks only: FCA's 1.0 hour to inspect and replace the lower radiator hose on a diesel Jeep Compass, FCA's 0.7 hour to inspect and replace a different coolant hose on a Dodge Durango 6.4L (both include an inspection and draining and refilling the coolant), and Volvo Trucks' 0.6 hour for the upper radiator hose on a highway tractor. These agree with the GM figure: roughly 0.6 to 1.0 hour as a warranty time. A GM bulletin for the 2023-2026 Colorado and Canyon names a labor operation for radiator inlet hose replacement but prints no time. Parts: each class now has a genuine list price and a name-brand aftermarket price from a second seller. The Ram low is on a page that says the part is new and lists the model years. The Corolla, Malibu and BMW lows are on ordinary new-parts retailer listings that name the model years but do not print the word 'new'; for the Corolla and the Malibu a second retailer's page for the same Gates part number says New (the Corolla hose is $13.19 there, without years). The Malibu 1.5L genuine hoses are unusually dear ($158.25 and $162.16 at list, against $45.68-$56.30 for the 2.0L and 2.5L cars), and the dealer catalog's titles disagree on which is the upper and which the lower. What is null and why: the top labor time for the BMW; no stated time for it was found and BMW time units were not converted. Benchmarks: Jerry $350-$630 (two hoses, 1 to 2.5 hours), RepairPal $304-$361 for the older Dodge Ram 1500 and $512-$547 for the later Ram 1500, YourMechanic about $251 on average. All three sit above the built totals for the cars and around the top of the truck's; that fits their covering both hoses, coolant or a flush, and longer labor times, and none says exactly what is included. So the built ranges are probably low for a real shop quote: they use a warranty add-on time and leave coolant out. Confidence is low: one class has no top labor time, only one labor figure in each of two classes is for the example vehicle, and the low labor time is a general guide. This is an estimate, not a quote and not a diagnosis.
extras: A quote often adds coolant (a top-up, or a full drain and refill; not included in this estimate), new clamps if they are not supplied with the hose, bleeding air from the cooling system, a cooling system pressure test, shop supplies and sales tax. Shops often recommend replacing the other radiator hose at the same time, and sometimes the thermostat, the radiator cap or a coolant flush; each is priced separately from this estimate. On vehicles with quick-connect hose fittings the hose comes as an assembly with its connectors and costs more than a plain hose. If the hose was replaced because of a leak or overheating, finding the cause is a separate diagnosis charge. A hose replaced under a recall, service campaign or warranty is done by the dealer at no charge, so check for open campaigns first.
